motivation: Miyasaka first used organic-inorganic lead halide perovskites as light absorbers in photovoltaic cells (2009). Park showed that these materials could be stable solid-state absorbers with efficiencies near 10% (2012). Snaith found that they carry charge over long distances in thin-film planar and meso-superstructured devices (2012–2013). Together they revealed a new class of solution-processed semiconductors with sharp absorption edges, low energetic disorder, tolerance of defects, mobile ions and diffusion lengths approaching a micron. These properties overturned long-held assumptions about how disordered, low-temperature-processed materials behave. Within a decade, single-junction efficiencies rose above 26% and perovskite-silicon tandems passed 34%, now moving toward commercial production. The discovery opened new physics of ion-electron coupling, polarons and defect tolerance. It also offers a credible route to cheaper, lower-carbon solar electricity at terawatt scale, a consequence that reaches well beyond the laboratory.
